canonical_title: Krishna Founds Dvaraka
variant_notes: BP 10.50 builds the fortress in the sea; VP 5.23 obtains twelve furlongs from the ocean and conducts the Yadavas thither.
notes: Harivamsha expands this into separate beats: the resolve to abandon Mathura (hv_a_001), site selection (hv_b1_113_02), Viswakarma's building (hv_b1_115_01), and enrichment (hv_b1_115_02).

canonical_title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini
variant_notes: BP 10.53 seizes her at the svayamvara after her temple prayer; VP 5.26 carries her off on the eve of her betrothal to Sisupala.

canonical_title: Krishna Defeats and Spares Rukmi
variant_notes: Harivamsha 1.116 has Rukmi vow to slay Krishna then duel near the Narmada; VP/BP have him pursue and be spared at Rukmini's plea.

canonical_title: Krishna Marries Rukmini
variant_notes: VP 5.26 bundles Pradyumna's birth with the marriage; Harivamsha notes Rukmini as first wife and mother of ten sons.

canonical_title: Shambara Steals the Infant Pradyumna
variant_notes: Age at abduction varies: six days (VP), seventh night (Harivamsha); BP just 'newborn'. All cast him into the sea.

canonical_title: Pradyumna Slays Shambara
variant_notes: BP: 'great science of countering illusion'; VP: slays the enchanter with his own eighth illusion.
notes: Harivamsha expands the duel into many beats (hv_b2_043-047).

canonical_title: Pradyumna Returns to Dvaraka and Is Recognized
variant_notes: Harivamsha has Rukmini recognize him by a dream and Vrishni marks; BP has her recognize her long-lost son.

canonical_title: Surya Grants Satrajit the Syamantaka Jewel
variant_notes: BP: jewel yields eight loads of gold daily; Harivamsha: Satrajit worships the sun on the ocean bank.

canonical_title: Prasena Is Slain by a Lion for the Jewel
variant_notes: BP 10.56 bundles Satrajit's refusal and the rumor blaming Krishna into the same beat; Harivamsha adds Jambavan killing the lion and taking the jewel.

canonical_title: Krishna Wrestles Jambavan for the Jewel
variant_notes: Duration varies: twenty-eight days (BP) vs twenty-one days (Harivamsha).

canonical_title: Krishna Returns the Jewel and Clears His Name
variant_notes: BP has him clear his name in open assembly and also receive Satyabhama.

canonical_title: Satadhanva Murders Satrajit for the Jewel
variant_notes: Harivamsha adds that Shatadhanwa secretly gives the jewel to Akrura; BP notes instigation by Akrura and Kritavarma.

canonical_title: Krishna Pursues and Slays Satadhanva
variant_notes: Both: killed near Mithila, no jewel found.
notes: Balarama's separate departure to Mithila is a distinct beat (hv_a_009).

canonical_title: Krishna Reclaims the Jewel from Akrura
variant_notes: Both have Krishna discern the jewel is with Akrura and return it to him after showing it in assembly.

canonical_title: Indra Reports Naraka's Tyranny and Asks Krishna's Help
variant_notes: VP lists Naraka's thefts (maidens, Varuna's umbrella, Aditi's earrings, demands Indra's elephant); Harivamsha has Indra descend and Krishna depart with Satyabhama on Garuda.

canonical_title: Krishna Slays Narakasura
variant_notes: Method: discus behead (BP), cut in two with discus (Harivamsha), cut nooses then slay (VP).
notes: Harivamsha bundles the slaying of Mura/generals; VP bundles freeing the captive princesses.

canonical_title: Krishna Frees the Sixteen Thousand Captive Maidens
variant_notes: Both: sixteen thousand maidens choose Krishna as husband.

canonical_title: Krishna Marries the Sixteen Thousand Princesses
variant_notes: Both: Krishna multiplies into 16,100 forms so each wife believes him hers alone.

canonical_title: Krishna Uproots the Parijata Tree from Indra's Heaven
variant_notes: BP 10.59 and Harivamsha 1.121 bundle the restoration of Aditi's earrings with the uprooting; bpc1_041 is Uddhava's recall.
notes: VP splits earrings-restoration (vp5_030_01) from the uprooting (vp5_030_02).

canonical_title: Indra and the Gods Contend with Krishna over the Parijata
variant_notes: VP: Krishna disarms all the gods with his discus and spares Indra; Harivamsha: Indra rides Airavata and challenges Krishna to battle.
notes: Harivamsha expands the battle (hv_b2_003-008); BP folds 'defeating the gods' into its uprooting beat.

canonical_title: Krishna Brings the Parijata to Satyabhama in Dvaraka
variant_notes: Harivamsha: Aditi grants it on condition of return; VP: planted in Satyabhama's garden.

canonical_title: Balarama Slays the Ape Dvivida
variant_notes: BP: Balarama fells him with his mace; VP: a single blow of the fist.
notes: The preceding ravages (bp10c_068) are a distinct beat.

canonical_title: Samba Carries Off Duryodhana's Daughter
variant_notes: Both: Samba abducts her at the svayamvara and is captured by the Kuru chiefs.

canonical_title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura with His Plough
variant_notes: All: Balarama hooks his plough under the city and threatens to fling it into the Ganga; the Kauravas yield Samba and the bride.

canonical_title: Shalva's Illusion of Vasudeva's Death
variant_notes: BP: Krishna briefly appears grief-stricken then sees through the sorcery; MB: Krishna swoons and drops the Sharnga bow.

canonical_title: Krishna Destroys the Flying City Saubha and Slays Shalva
variant_notes: MB splits it: discus cuts Saubha in twain (mb_a2_027), then cleaves Salwa (mb_a2_028); BP bundles both (mace shatters Saubha, discus beheads Shalva).

canonical_title: The Sages Curse Samba and the Yadavas
variant_notes: bpc1_009 extends to the iron mace appearing, being ground and cast into the sea; bpc1_046 is Uddhava's recall; VP 5.37 states the iron-club curse plainly.

canonical_title: Krishna and Arjuna Journey to Recover the Brahmana's Sons
variant_notes: BP: divine chariot beyond the darkness to Vaikuntha; Harivamsha: across the ocean and the seven cosmic mountains.

canonical_title: The Brahmana's Sons Are Restored
variant_notes: BP: the Supreme Lord returns the children; Harivamsha: three stolen boys and the new-born infant restored.

canonical_title: Usha Dreams of Aniruddha
variant_notes: Both: Usha dreams of the youth and Chitralekha paints the princes until she recognizes Aniruddha.

canonical_title: Aniruddha Is Brought to Usha and They Unite
variant_notes: BP: Chitralekha carries the sleeping Aniruddha to Shonitapura; Harivamsha: they are united in secret Gandharva marriage.

canonical_title: Bana Captures and Binds Aniruddha
variant_notes: BP and VP: bound with serpent-nooses; Harivamsha: fettered with serpentine shafts via Tamasika illusion.
notes: Aniruddha's rout of Vana's soldiers (hv_b2_057) and Durga's later release (hv_b2_059) are distinct beats.

canonical_title: Krishna Stupefies Shiva and Puts Skanda to Flight
variant_notes: BP: Jrimbhana astra; VP: weapon of yawning. VP bundles the three-headed Fever's defeat here.
notes: The Jvara/Fever episode is expanded in Harivamsha (hv_b2_063-066).

canonical_title: Krishna and Shiva Duel with Divine Weapons
variant_notes: BP: Krishna repels Shiva's celestial weapons; Harivamsha: exchange of Indra/Shiva/Varuna/Vaishnava weapons.

canonical_title: Krishna Severs Bana's Thousand Arms and Spares Him
variant_notes: Arms remaining varies: four (BP) vs two (Harivamsha/VP). Shiva intercedes in all.
notes: Bana's subsequent dance and Mahakala boon (hv_b2_074) is a distinct beat.

canonical_title: Aniruddha and Usha Are Freed
variant_notes: BP: Bana surrenders and hands them over; Harivamsha: the serpent-bonds fall away at the sight of Garuda.

canonical_title: Balarama Marries Revati
variant_notes: Harivamsha: weds Revati, daughter of king Revata; VP: after sporting two months in Vraja, marries Revati daughter of Raivata.

canonical_title: Aniruddha Is Betrothed to Rukmi's Granddaughter
variant_notes: Both: Aniruddha wed to Rukmi's granddaughter, celebrated at Bhojakata.

canonical_title: Balarama Slays Rukmi at the Dice Game
variant_notes: Weapon varies: iron club (BP), dice-board (Harivamsha). VP adds a heavenly voice confirms the foul play.

canonical_title: Krishna Slays Paundraka and the King of Kashi
variant_notes: Both: impostor Paundraka beheaded, Kashi king's head cast/shot into his own city.
notes: Paundraka's false claim (bp10c_065) is a distinct beat.

canonical_title: Sudarshana Consumes the Conjured Fire and Burns Varanasi/Benares
variant_notes: BP: Sudakshina conjures the fiery demon; VP: the son of the slain Kashi king conjures the fiend.

canonical_title: Krishna Wins Lakshmana at Her Svayamvara
variant_notes: bp10d_039 gives Lakshmana's own account (strung a bow, shot the fish target); bp10c_040 bundles her abduction with Bhadra's marriage.

canonical_title: Kalayavana Is Burned by Muchukunda's Glance || Krishna lures Kalayavana into Muchukunda's cave; the Yavana kicks the sleeping king and is reduced to ashes.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: VP aftermath vp5_024_01 (Krishna seizes Kalayavana's host).

canonical_title: Muchukunda's Story || Muchukunda, an Ikshvaku king who once guarded the gods against the asuras, was granted deep sleep as his reward.
variant_notes: BP-only beat; immediately precedes the boon (bp10c_015).

canonical_title: Krishna Grants Muchukunda His Boon || Krishna reveals himself to Muchukunda, who renounces all boons and asks only for devotion; Krishna grants him liberation in a future birth.
variant_notes: BP-only beat; follows Muchukunda's story (bp10c_014).

canonical_title: Krishna and Balarama Elude Jarasandha || Krishna and Balarama feign flight from Jarasandha, escape to Dvaraka over the sea, and Jarasandha falsely believes them burned.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Harivamsha resolve to abandon Mathura (hv_a_001) and the founding (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02).

canonical_title: Rukmini Resolves to Marry Krishna and Sends a Brahmana Messenger || Princess Rukmini, hearing of Krishna's virtues, resolves to wed him and sends a brahmana to Dvaraka with her secret message.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster (bp10c_021/vp5_026_01); message is bp10c_018.

canonical_title: Rukmini's Love-Message to Krishna || Rukmini's message begs Krishna to carry her away in the rakshasa manner before Shishupala can claim her.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster; resolve is bp10c_017.

canonical_title: Krishna Hastens to Kundina || Krishna receives Rukmini's message and races overnight to Kundina, where rival kings are gathering to enforce Shishupala's claim.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster (bp10c_021/vp5_026_01).

canonical_title: Rukmini's Prayer at the Temple of Ambika || Anxious at Krishna's delay, Rukmini visits the temple of goddess Ambika and prays that Krishna alone may be her husband.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Rukmini abduction cluster; distinct prayer beat.

canonical_title: Mayavati (Rati) Rescues and Raises Pradyumna || A fish swallows the infant; a cook finds him, and Mayavati, who is Rati, recognizes Kama reborn and raises him as her own.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Shambara-stole cluster (bp10c_024); Harivamsha expands (hv_b2_042-047).

canonical_title: Satyabhama Reports Her Father's Murder || Satyabhama finds her father slain, and hastens to Hastinapura to tell Krishna, who laments with Balarama.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Satadhanva cluster (bp10c_032/hv_a_007).

canonical_title: Krishna Abducts Mitravinda and Wins Satya || Krishna carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara and wins Satya of Kosala by taming seven fierce bulls.
variant_notes: Bundles two moments (Mitravinda + Satya); cross-ref bpc1_040 for the Satya recall.

canonical_title: Krishna Breaches Mura's Fortifications || Indra complains of Narakasura's thefts; Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda shatters the mountain, weapon, water, fire and Mura-pasha defenses of Pragjyotisha.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Naraka cluster; distinct fortification-breach beat (Mura's defenses).

canonical_title: Krishna Slays Mura and His Seven Sons || Krishna beheads the five-headed demon Mura and slays his seven sons who attack in revenge.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Naraka cluster (hv_b1_120_02 bundles Mura's slaying).

canonical_title: Bhumi Returns Aditi's Earrings || The earth-goddess Bhumi restores Aditi's earrings and Varuna's umbrella and prays for the protection of Naraka's son Bhagadatta.
variant_notes: Distinct: Bhumi (earth-goddess) restores the treasures; cross-ref Krishna's earrings restoration (vp5_030_01).

canonical_title: Krishna Jests with Rukmini || Krishna playfully tells Rukmini she chose a poor, unworthy husband; she faints in grief, thinking he means to abandon her.
variant_notes: BP-only; paired with consolation beat (bp10c_049).

canonical_title: Krishna Consoles Rukmini || Krishna lifts Rukmini, reveals his jest, praises her devotion, and the two are reconciled in love.
variant_notes: BP-only; paired with jest beat (bp10c_048).

canonical_title: Bana's Thousand Arms and Shiva's Boon || The thousand-armed asura Bana, son of Bali and devotee of Shiva, wins the boon of a worthy rival in battle.
variant_notes: BP-only background beat for the Bana episode.

canonical_title: Krishna Liberates King Nriga from a Lizard's Body || The Yadu princes find a giant lizard in a well; Krishna pulls it out with his left hand, and it becomes the radiant King Nriga.
variant_notes: BP-only; Nriga episode has no cross-source parallel in this chunk.

canonical_title: Nriga's Story of the Disputed Cow || Nriga, an Ikshvaku king famed for charity, tells how he unwittingly gave one brahmana's stray cow to another and was cursed to become a lizard.
variant_notes: BP-only; follows bp10c_060.

canonical_title: Nriga Ascends and Krishna Warns Against Stealing Brahmanas' Wealth || Touched by Krishna, Nriga ascends to heaven in a celestial car, and Krishna warns the citizens that a brahmana's property is deadly poison.
variant_notes: BP-only; follows bp10c_061.

canonical_title: Balarama Visits the Gopis of Gokula || Balarama returns to Nanda's Gokula, consoles the pining gopis with Krishna's message, and stays two months in their company.
variant_notes: BP-only; Balarama's Gokula visit.

canonical_title: Balarama Drags the Yamuna with His Plough || Intoxicated by Varuni, Balarama summons the Yamuna to sport; when she refuses, he drags her with his plough until she begs forgiveness.
variant_notes: BP-only; Balarama drags the Yamuna (distinct from dragging Hastinapura).

canonical_title: Paundraka Falsely Claims to Be Vasudeva || Paundraka, king of Karusha, proclaims himself the true Vasudeva and sends a messenger demanding that Krishna surrender his divine insignia.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Paundraka-slaying cluster (bp10c_066/vp5_034_01).

canonical_title: The Gorilla Dvivida Ravages the Land || The gorilla Dvivida, Narakasura's friend, wreaks havoc on the countryside in revenge, burning villages, drowning lands and defiling sages' hermitages.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Dvivida-slaying cluster (bp10c_069/vp5_036_01).

canonical_title: Balarama Seeks Samba's Release and Is Insulted || Balarama goes to Hastinapura as peacemaker, but the Kauravas, drunk on pride, mock the Yadavas and refuse to release Samba.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Balarama-drags-Hastinapura cluster (bp10c_072).

canonical_title: Narada Sees Krishna in Every Palace of Dvaraka || Narada visits Dvaraka to witness Krishna's household, and sees him simultaneously present in each of the 16,000 palaces performing different duties.
Narada Marvels at Krishna's Yoga-Maya and Departs || Narada praises Krishna's unfathomable yoga-maya, and Krishna bids him wander singing his glories throughout the worlds.
Krishna's Dawn Worship in Dwaraka || Krishna rises in the brahma-muhurta, performs his ablutions, worships the Lord within, gives daily gifts of cows and wealth to brahmanas, and blesses his people.

The Captive Kings Appeal to Krishna || A royal messenger arrives in Krishna's assembly and reports that Jarasandha has imprisoned twenty thousand defeated kings in Girivraja, who beg Krishna for release.

Uddhava's Counsel to Slay Jarasandha || Uddhava advises Krishna that the Rajasuya requires conquering the directions, and that Jarasandha — who can only be killed by Bhima in single combat — must first be destroyed.
Krishna's Grand Procession from Dwaraka || Krishna departs Dwaraka for Indraprastha with a vast army, chariots, elephants and his queens, to the sound of drums and conches.
Approaching Jarasandha in Disguise || Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna travel to Girivraja disguised as brahmanas and ask Jarasandha for alms, testing his charity.
Jarasandha Taunts Krishna || Krishna reveals their true identities and asks for single combat; Jarasandha laughs, taunts Krishna as a coward who fled Mathura, and chooses Bhima as his opponent.
The Mace-Duel of Bhima and Jarasandha || Bhima and Jarasandha fight an indecisive mace-duel, exchanging blows that crush their clubs, then striking with iron-hard fists.
Krishna's Signal: Jarasandha Split in Two || Knowing Jarasandha's birth secret, Krishna signals by splitting a twig; Bhima tears Jarasandha in two and kills him.
Sahadeva Crowned and the Kings Freed || Krishna crowns Jarasandha's son Sahadeva king of Magadha and releases all the kings imprisoned by Jarasandha.
The Liberated Kings Behold Krishna || Twenty thousand eight hundred freed kings emerge from the mountain prison, behold Krishna's form, praise him, receive his teaching, and are sent home with honor.
Shalva Wins the Flying City Saubha || Shalva, friend of the slain Shishupala, vows to destroy the Yadavas and wins from Shiva through austere penance the flying iron city Saubha, built by Maya.
Shalva Besieges Dwaraka || Shalva arrives at Dwaraka in the indestructible flying city Saubha and rains weapons, rocks and serpents upon the city, terrifying its people.

Pradyumna's Valor and Wounding || Pradyumna destroys Shalva's illusions and slays many foes, but is struck senseless by Dyuman's mace; recovering, he rebukes his charioteer for drawing him from the field.
Krishna Returns to the Battle || Returning from Indraprastha and seeing evil omens, Krishna hurries to Dwaraka, orders his chariot against Shalva, and joins the fight, shattering Shalva's weapons.
Krishna Slays Dantavakra and Viduratha || Dantavakra attacks Krishna with a mace to avenge Shishupala and Shalva; Krishna crushes his chest, then beheads his brother Viduratha with the discus.

Balarama Slays the Suta Romaharshana || At Naimisha, Balarama, seeing the suta Romaharshana seated without rising to honor the sages, kills him with a blade of kusha grass; the sages cry out that he has committed brahma-hatya.

The Sages Prescribe Balarama's Penance || The sages instruct Balarama that to expiate the brahmana-slaying he must slay the demon Balvala, who defiles their sacrifice, and then perform a year-long pilgrimage.

Balarama Slays the Demon Balvala || When Balvala appears at the sacrifice raining impurity, Balarama drags him down with his plough and crushes his head with his mace, and the sages shower Balarama with honors.
Sudama's Poverty and Journey || Sudama's wife urges the destitute brahmana to seek his boyhood friend Krishna, and he sets out for Dwaraka with a humble gift of flat rice.
Krishna Embraces His Old Friend || Krishna rises from his couch, embraces Sudama with tears of joy, washes his feet, and anoints him, while Rukmini fans him, astonishing the palace women.

Memories of the Gurukula || Krishna and Sudama recall their student days under Sandipani, when they were sent to fetch firewood and, caught in a fierce storm, wandered lost until the guru found them at dawn.
Krishna Eats Sudama's Flat Rice || Krishna asks for the gift and eats Sudama's handful of flat rice with delight, and Sudama, too ashamed to ask for anything, returns home empty-handed.
Sudama Finds His Hut a Palace || Returning home, Sudama finds his poor dwelling transformed into a celestial palace and his wife radiant, and he reflects that this is Krishna's unasked grace.
The Brahmana's Dying Sons || In Dwaraka, a brahmana's newborn sons die one after another; he lays their bodies at the palace gate and laments the king's failure to protect his subjects.
Arjuna's Failed Vow || Arjuna boasts that he will protect the brahmana's next child, but though he fences the delivery-room with arrows, the newborn vanishes, and the brahmana rebukes him.

Krishna Carries Off Rukmini and Wins Satya || Uddhava recalls how Krishna carried off Rukmini, Bhishmaka's daughter, by the gandharva rite, and how he defeated the proud kings to win Satya (Nagnajiti) at her svayamvara.
variant_notes: Recall bundling Rukmini's abduction + Satya's svayamvara; cross-ref both clusters.

canonical_title: Krishna Slays Narakasura and Weds the Sixteen Thousand || Uddhava recalls how Krishna slew the demon Naraka (Bhauma), who had seized the earth's princesses, and how the freed princesses chose Krishna as their husband, who married them all in one moment and begot sons in each.
variant_notes: Recall bundling Naraka's slaying + the 16,000 marriages; cross-ref both clusters.

canonical_title: Krishna Defeats the Besieging Kings and Demons || Uddhava recalls how Krishna destroyed the hosts of Kala, Magadha (Jarasandha) and Shalva that besieged Dwaraka, and slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others.
variant_notes: Recall bundling many battles (Kala, Magadha, Shalva, Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra).

canonical_title: Krishna Foresees the Yadavas' Self-Destruction || Uddhava recalls Krishna's deliberation that the Yadu warriors, themselves the remaining burden of the earth, could be destroyed in no other way than by their own quarrel, and that when he acted, they would destroy themselves.
variant_notes: Recall; cross-ref the Yadavas' self-destruction (vp5_037_03).

canonical_title: The Vrishnis Resolve to Abandon Mathura for Dwarka || Fearing Kalayavana's assault, the Vrishnis and Andhakas make Krishna their president and resolve to leave Mathura for Kushasthali (Dwarka).
variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02); distinct resolve-to-depart beat.

canonical_title: The Vrishnis Suspect Krishna of Stealing the Jewel || Hearing of Prasena's death, the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspect Krishna of stealing the Syamantaka; the innocent Krishna resolves to recover it.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Prasena cluster (bp10c_029/hv_a_003); distinct accusation beat.

canonical_title: Balarama Departs to Mithila in Anger || Believing Krishna is withholding the jewel, Balarama angrily leaves for Mithila, where Duryodhana learns the use of clubs from him.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Satadhanva cluster (bp10c_034/hv_a_008).

canonical_title: Akrura's Exile Brings Drought; His Return Brings Rain || After Akrura leaves Dwarka, Indra withholds rain and drought devastates the land; when he returns, the rains fall again.
variant_notes: Harivamsha-only; Akrura's exile/drought episode.

canonical_title: Krishna Selects the Site of Dwaraka || The Yadavas reach the ocean shore, and Krishna, seeking a place to build, chooses the coppery tract near Mount Raivata where the Yadavas encamp.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster (bp10c_012/vp5_023_02); site-selection beat.

canonical_title: Viswakarma Builds Dwaraka || Krishna summons the divine architect Viswakarma, and after the ocean withdraws twelve yojanas, the celestial city of Dwaravati is raised.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster; Viswakarma's building beat.

canonical_title: Krishna Enriches Dwaraka || Krishna bids the treasure-guard Sankha shower wealth on every household and sends Vayu to fetch the celestial assembly-hall Sudharma from heaven.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: founding cluster; enrichment beat.

canonical_title: Rukmavati's Swayamvara and Marriage || Rukmi's daughter Rukmavati chooses Pradyumna at her swayamvara; later her son Aniruddha is wed to Rukmavati's namesake, the granddaughter of Rukmi.
variant_notes: Cross-ref: Aniruddha nuptials (bp10c_050/vp5_028_01) and Pradyumna's marriage to Rukmavati.

canonical_title: Narada Presents the Parijata Flower to Rukmini || Narada gives Krishna a Parijata flower, which Krishna passes to Rukmini; the sage extols Rukmini as the foremost of his wives.

Satyabhama Is Consumed by Jealousy || Satyabhama's maids report Rukmini's good fortune; the proud queen, unable to bear her co-wife's honor, casts off her ornaments and retires to the apartment of anger.
Krishna Consoles the Jealous Satyabhama || Krishna steals into Satyabhama's chamber and, fanning her and wiping her tears, protests that his love dwells in her alone.
Krishna Promises Satyabhama the Parijata Tree || Satyabhama confesses her grief over the Parijata flower given to Rukmini; Krishna vows to fetch the whole Parijata tree from Indra's heaven for her.
Krishna Sends Narada to Ask Indra for the Parijata || Krishna asks Narada to request the Parijata tree from Indra as a brotherly favour, and warns that if refused he will come himself to seize it.

Indra Refuses and Challenges Krishna || Narada relays Krishna's demand; Indra, recounting past grievances, refuses to part with the Parijata tree unless conquered in battle and sends back a challenge.
Pradyumna Duels Jayanta in the Sky || Pradyumna, son of Rukmini, battles Indra's son Jayanta; a heavenly weapon burns Pradyumna's chariot to ashes yet cannot harm him, who stands firm in the sky.

Satyaki Fights the Brahmana Pravara; Garuda Strikes Him Down || Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him; when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.

Garuda Fells Airavata from Heaven || Garuda fights Indra's elephant Airavata, striking it with claws and talons until the wounded elephant falls from the heights of heaven onto the Parijatra mountain.

Krishna Worships Shiva and Wins His Boon || Pausing the fight at nightfall, Krishna performs ablutions in the Ganga, eulogizes Shiva with a hymn, and Shiva appears with Uma, granting that he shall carry away the Parijata and remain invincible.

Shiva Reveals the Danava Stronghold of Satpura || Shiva tells Krishna of the Danavas hidden in the Satpura stronghold beneath the mountain — invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon — and Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain.
Kashyapa and Aditi Reconcile Krishna and Indra || Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two 'brothers' lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled.

Satyabhama's Punyaka Rite and the Gift to Narada || Satyabhama binds Krishna to the Parijata, dedicates him to the sage Narada, and gifts gold, kine and jewels; Narada releases him for a fee, and Satyabhama distributes celestial garments to the sixteen thousand wives.

Krishna Returns the Parijata and Vows to Destroy the Danavas || After a year of festival, Krishna returns the Parijata to heaven, and before Indra vows to slay, within ten days, the Danavas that the gods cannot kill.

The Danavas Demand a Share of Brahmadatta's Yajna || At the Brahmana Brahmadatta's year-long sacrifice in Shatpura, the Danava Nikumbha and his kin demand Soma, jewels and the Brahmana's daughters, threatening to disrupt the rite.

Pradyumna Saves the Maidens by Illusion || When the Danavas scatter the sacrifice and carry off Brahmadatta's daughters, Pradyumna, sent by Krishna, rescues the maidens by illusion, leaving only counterfeit figures for the demons.

Narada Incites the Kings to Aid the Asuras || Narada, foreseeing a clash at the crowded sacrifice, prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas — while warning the Pandavas to hold back.

Nikumbha Imprisons the Yadava Heroes by Maya || Using his illusive powers, Nikumbha carries Anadhrishti, Kritavarma, Charudeshna and many other Yadavas one by one into the Shatpura cave and imprisons them, enraging Krishna and Baladeva.

Krishna Routs the Asuras with the Sarnga Bow || Krishna, with his Sarnga bow, consumes the Danava host like fire on grass, while Jayanta and Pravara slay from the sky every Asura who tries to escape upward.

Pradyumna Binds the Bribed Kings with Shiva's Nooses || Bearing nooses given by Hara and commanded by Nandi, Pradyumna binds Sisupala, Bhagadatta, Rukmi and the other kings who sided with the Asuras, and holds them in the illusory cave.

Krishna Slays Nikumbha with the Sudarshana Discus || As the routed Asuras return to fight, Krishna follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana.

Krishna Distributes the Spoils and Grants Shatpura to Brahmadatta || After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta.

Krishna Sports with His Sixteen Thousand Wives in the Ocean || Sailing to the shrine of Pindaraka, the Yadavas sport in the ocean; Krishna sports simultaneously with his sixteen thousand wives, each believing she alone is his favourite, while he makes the salt ocean sweet.

Krishna Brings the Celestial Chhalikya Song to the Yadavas || Krishna stages a music soiree: Narada plays the vina, Krishna dances the Hallishaka with his flute, and the Apsaras Rambha and Urvashi perform, as the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind.

Nikumbha Carries Away Bhanumati || While the Yadavas are absorbed in ocean sport, the Danava Nikumbha, avenging Pradyumna's earlier abduction of Prabhavati, steals Bhānu's daughter Bhanumati from her unguarded garden.

Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna Pursue the Abductor || Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna overtake Nikumbha on Garuda; careful not to wound the maiden, they pierce him with cane-like arrows as he flees across the earth, and Pradyumna recovers Bhanumati.

Nikumbha Fells Arjuna and Pradyumna; Krishna Duels Him || Emerging from the Shatpura cave, Nikumbha knocks Arjuna and Pradyumna senseless with his thorned club; enraged, Krishna seizes Kaumodaki and fights him in single combat.

Krishna Destroys a Body of Nikumbha with the Discus || As Nikumbha's illusion fills earth and sky with a thousand of his forms, Krishna, perceiving the true form with celestial wisdom, cuts off its head with his discus and frees the abducted Arjuna.

Narada Reveals Bhanumati's Fate; She Weds Sahadeva || Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages; Bhānu then gives her in marriage to Sahadeva.

Vajranabha Wins His Boon and Demands the Three Worlds || By austerities on Sumeru, the Asura Vajranabha wins from Brahma the unconquerable city Vajra and immunity from the gods, then challenges Indra for the sovereignty of the three worlds.

Krishna's Stratagem: the Actor Bhadra and the Swan Emissaries || Indra consults Krishna, who promises to slay Vajranabha after Vasudeva's horse-sacrifice; an actor named Bhadra wins a boon of entering the impenetrable city, and Indra sends swans to win Prabhavati for Pradyumna.

The Yadavas Enter Vajra Disguised as Actors || Disguised as actors, the Yadavas enter Vajranabha's impenetrable city and perform the Ramayana and Rambhabhisara so skilfully that the Danavas shower them with jewels until their own wealth is drained.

Pradyumna in Bee Form Meets Prabhavati || Pradyumna, aided by Prabhavati's goose friend Suchimukhi, assumes the form of a bee hidden in a flower-garland, alights on Prabhavati's ear, and the long-pining lovers meet by night.

Kashyapa Warns Vajranabha, Who Marches on Heaven || After Kashyapa's sacrifice, Vajranabha rejects his father's warning that he cannot vanquish Indra and sets out with his kinsmen to conquer the celestial region.

The Danava Princesses Arm Their Yadava Husbands || When Vajranabha orders the arrest of the young Yadava sons, Prabhavati hands Pradyumna a sword and blesses him with victory, while Chandravati and Gunavati arm Gada and Shamba.

Pradyumna Fights with Ananta as Charioteer || Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.
Pradyumna Duels Vajranabha || Riding Garuda, Pradyumna wounds Vajranabha, who in turn fells him with a club; the sound of Krishna's Panchajanya conch revives the fallen hero.

Pradyumna Slays Vajranabha with Krishna's Discus || Krishna's discus comes into Pradyumna's hand, and with it he severs Vajranabha's head, while Gada slays Sunabha and Shamba destroys the remaining Asuras.

Indra and Krishna Install the Four Young Kings || Indra and Krishna divide Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts and anoint the four young princes — Vijaya and the sons of Pradyumna, Shamba and Gada — as kings of the Vajra realm.

Vishwakarma Adorns Dwarka for Krishna || At Indra's request, the celestial architect Vishwakarma beautifies Dwarka after Amaravati, building golden palaces for each of Krishna's queens, and Krishna enters the adorned city.

Krishna Returns to Dwarka and Honors Naraka's Captive Maidens || Krishna re-enters Dwarka with the Parijata and the treasure-mountain, blows the Panchajanya to the citizens' joy, and honors the maidens freed from Naraka's house with garments, riches and homes.

The Yogamaya Appears Before Krishna and Rama || The illusory daughter of Yashoda — the goddess born the same moment as Krishna — appears before Krishna and Rama, who embrace her and seat her between them as the Vrishni women worship her.

Narada Prophesies the Ocean Will Swallow Dwarka || Before departing, Narada prophesies that Krishna, having fulfilled the gods' work, will let the ocean inundate Dwarka and Bhogavati, and will be united with Narayana.

Mayavati Reveals the Truth to Pradyumna || When the grown Pradyumna recoils at Mayavati's advances, she reveals he is not her son but the child of Rukmini and Vasudeva, stolen by Shamvara, and that she is his former wife.

Pradyumna Fells Shamvara's Standard to Provoke Him || To draw out the Danava who stole him, Pradyumna strikes down Shamvara's lion-emblazoned standard, and the enraged Shamvara sends his hundred sons to kill him.
Pradyumna Slays the Hundred Sons of Shamvara || In a single battle, Pradyumna cuts down all hundred of Shamvara's sons who come against him, and stands victorious awaiting the father.
Pradyumna Slays Shamvara's Four Ministers || Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — one by one, and their army flees in terror.

Shamvara's Illusions and Pradyumna's Counters || Shamvara hurls illusory trees, stones, lions and a serpent-maya at Pradyumna, who counters each with fiery weapons and a Garuda illusion, to the applause of the gods.

Narada Reveals Pradyumna's True Identity and Arms Him || Sent by Indra, Narada reminds Pradyumna of his former birth as Kama, gives him the Vaishnava weapons and a coat of mail, and bids him slay Shamvara and reclaim his wife Mayavati.

Narada's Riddle: Who Is Truly Great || When Narada cryptically hails Krishna as 'wonder and blessed' and Krishna answers 'presents', the puzzled kings ask the meaning; Narada recounts a journey from tortoise to Ganga, ocean, earth, mountains, Brahma, the Vedas and the Yajnas, each deferring to the next, until the riddle resolves in Vishnu with dakshina.
Krishna Marches on Sonitpura in Divine Form || To rescue Aniruddha from Bana, Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna fly out on Garuda, Krishna assuming eight arms and innumerable heads with his weapons.

Garuda Quenches Bana's Protective Fire || As Bana's city-fire blazes out and robs the Yadavas of their lustre, Garuda assumes a thousand mouths, drinks the etherial Ganga and showers it down to extinguish the flames.

Krishna Strikes Down Angira and the Fire-Gods || Bana's fire-gods, led by the chief Angira, attack Krishna on the way, and Krishna, cutting off Angira's mace, fells him with an arrow, putting the rest to flight.

Chitralekha Comes to Dwarka as Usha's Emissary || Usha's friend Chitralekha travels to Dwarka to bring Aniruddha back for her mistress, and secures Narada's blessing and the Tamasika power of illusion to carry out the abduction.

Aniruddha Routs Vana's Soldiers || When Vana discovers Usha living with Aniruddha and sends his soldiers to kill him, Aniruddha seizes a Parigha and single-handedly drives the Danava host from the field.

The Goddess Durga Releases Aniruddha from His Bonds || Imprisoned in Vana's city, Aniruddha hymns the goddess Katyayani, and Durga appears, cuts the serpent-nooses with her fingers, and consoles him, promising Krishna will sever Vana's thousand arms.

The Yadavas' Grief and Search for Aniruddha || Aniruddha's wives lament and the whole Yadava assembly falls into grief; Krishna broods over the disappearance, and messengers are sent out to search mountains, forests and every country in vain.

Narada Reveals Aniruddha's Captivity by Vana || Narada arrives at the anxious court and tells Krishna that Vana's daughter Usha, with Chitralekha, took Aniruddha, that Vana bound him with serpent-shafts, and that he lives imprisoned awaiting rescue.

Krishna Summons Garuda and Marches to Rescue Aniruddha || At Narada's bidding, Krishna summons Garuda, mounts his back with Baladeva and Pradyumna, and sets out for the distant city of Sonitpura to free Aniruddha.

Jvara Consumes Baladeva; Krishna Saves Him || The fever-demon Jvara, with three legs, three heads and six arms, hurls a burning weapon that consumes Baladeva; Krishna embraces his brother and by his touch saves him from being burnt.
Krishna Grapples with Jvara || Krishna challenges Jvara and, bearing the demon's burning weapon and blows, grinds him with his arms in a fearful struggle.

Jvara Possesses Krishna; Krishna Expels Him || The released Jvara enters Krishna's body and enfeebles him; Krishna creates a dreadful counter-Jvara from his own energy, which seizes and drags the fever out of his body.

Krishna Spares Jvara and Grants Him Boons || Commanded by an invisible voice, Krishna spares Jvara and grants him boons — that he alone be the world's fever, divided into forms to afflict beasts, plants and mankind.
Shiva and Kartikeya Enter the Battle for Vana || As Vana's army flees, Shiva, eyes red with anger, ascends his lion-drawn car surrounded by his ghostly host, and Kartikeya joins him to protect Vana.

Kartikeya Duels the Yadavas; Krishna Counters Brahmashira || Kartikeya rides out and strikes Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna; when he discharges the world-destroying Brahmashira weapon, Krishna's discus blots out its lustre, and he strikes down Kartikeya's burning Sakti.

Kottavi Intervenes to Save Kartikeya || As Krishna raises his discus against Kartikeya, the naked goddess Kottavi, sent by Mahadeva, intervenes, and Krishna, unable to strike before her, puts away his discus.

Vana Vaunts and Fights Krishna || Vana boasts of his thousand arms, but Krishna answers and, with the Sarnga bow, sunders Vana's car, horses and standard, then strips him of crown, mail, bow and shield until he swoons.

Kottavi Again Intercedes; Krishna Vows to Cut Vana's Arms || When the naked goddess Kottavi again stands between them to honour her boon of protection to Vana, Krishna vows to cut off Vana's thousand arms, leaving only two, while sparing his life.

Shiva Intercedes for Vana; Vana Dances and Wins Boons || Shiva intercedes for Vana's life, Krishna withdraws his discus, and the armless Vana, bidden by Nandi, dances before Shiva and receives boons, becoming the Pramatha chief Mahakala.

Krishna Celebrates Aniruddha's Wedding and Grants the Kingdom to Kumbhanda || Krishna celebrates Aniruddha and Usha's wedding, and confers Vana's kingdom on the minister Kumbhanda, who had counselled mercy toward Aniruddha.

Krishna Fights Varuna for the Celestial Cows || Seeking Vana's celestial kine in Varuna's charge for Satyabhama, Krishna routs Varuna's army and battles Varuna, whose Varuna-weapon is consumed by Krishna's Vaishnava weapon.

Varuna Pleads His Promise; Krishna Relents || Varuna pleads his vow to Vana never to part with the cows, and Krishna, honouring his truthfulness, releases both Varuna and the cows and returns to Dwarka amid the rejoicing citizens.

Usha Is Welcomed into the Yadu Family || Back in Dwarka, Ahuka bids a festival; Usha is conducted to Aniruddha's house amid benedictions, and Devaki, Revati and Rukmini welcome her with tears of joy, closing the Vana episode.

Krishna Shatters the Rock-Shower with Indra's Thunderbolt || Buried under torrents of rocks hurled by Salwa's Danavas, Krishna wields Indra's thunderbolt and destroys the entire mass of crags, then resumes the fight.

Krishna Seizes Kalayavana's Host || Having destroyed Kalayavana by stratagem, Krishna captures his army of horses, elephants and cars, and delivers it to Ugrasena, freeing the Yadava race from fear of invasion.
Krishna Restores Aditi's Earrings || Krishna restores the recovered earrings to Aditi, who blesses him; Satyabhama is promised unfading beauty.

canonical_title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Badarikashrama || Seeing the omens of Dwaraka's doom, Krishna bids Uddhava depart to the shrine of Naranarayana at Badarikashrama, where by meditating on Krishna he shall attain perfection.

The Yadavas Destroy One Another || At Prabhasa the Yadava chiefs, inflamed by liquor, fall upon one another; the rushes in their hands become thunderbolts, and nearly the whole race perishes, even Krishna slaying many with an iron club.
Sesha Departs from Balarama || As Krishna watches, the great serpent Sesha issues from Balarama's mouth and enters the ocean, hymned by saints and serpents, and Ocean comes forth to receive him.
